title: Video to GIF – Make an Animated GIF from a Clip Free
description: Turn up to 30 seconds of an MP4, MOV or WebM video into an animated GIF. Pick the width and frames per second; nothing is uploaded.
heading: Convert Video to GIF
subtitle: Pick a start and an end, a width and a frame rate, and get an animated GIF made in your browser.
intro: A GIF plays on its own, loops, and works in chats, emails, slides and pages that don't take video. Choose the moment you want, up to 30 seconds, a width from 240 to 640 pixels and 5 to 20 frames per second. The page counts the frames before you start, so you know how big the GIF will be, and shows the result before you download it.

features.title: Private
features.text: Your clip is turned into a GIF by your own browser; the video never leaves your device.

features.title: You choose the size
features.text: Width and frames per second decide how smooth and how large the GIF is; the page counts the frames for you.

features.title: See it first
features.text: The GIF plays on the page before you download it, so you can try another part or setting.

stepsTitle: How to make a GIF from a video

steps.title: Add your video
steps.text: Choose or drop an MP4, MOV, WebM or MKV file. The first 5 seconds are chosen for you.

steps.title: Pick the part
steps.text: Type a start and an end, up to 30 seconds apart, and choose the width and frames per second.

steps.title: Make the GIF
steps.text: Click Make GIF, watch it play on the page and download it.

handles: Videos: MP4, MOV, WebM, MKV and other files your browser can play.
Length: up to 30 seconds from anywhere in the video.
Width: 240, 320, 480 or 640 pixels; the height follows the video's shape, and a small video is never enlarged.
Frame rate: 5, 10, 15 or 20 frames per second, with up to 256 colours per frame.
limits: A GIF is at most 30 seconds long. Every frame is stored as a whole picture, so long GIFs become very large.
GIFs have no sound and at most 256 colours per frame, so smooth gradients can look banded.
Above about 300 frames the page warns you: the GIF may be slow to make and large to send.

faq.question: Is my video uploaded?
faq.answer: No. Your browser reads the video and draws the GIF on your device; nothing is sent anywhere. You can check it in your browser's network panel.

faq.question: Why is a GIF limited to 30 seconds?
faq.answer: A GIF stores every frame as a full picture, without the clever compression video uses. Thirty seconds at 15 frames per second is already 450 pictures, which can be tens of megabytes.

faq.question: How do I make the GIF smaller?
faq.answer: Use a shorter part, a smaller width or fewer frames per second. 320 pixels at 10 frames per second suits most chats.

faq.question: Does the GIF keep the sound?
faq.answer: No, GIFs can't hold sound. To keep the sound, trim the video instead, or save its sound with Video to MP3.

faq.question: Which browsers does it work in?
faq.answer: Recent Chrome and Edge read and make the most formats; Safari and Firefox work with most videos. If your browser can't read or make a codec, the page names it and says what to try instead.
